The Board reminds owners of residential and commercial premises with water storage tanks to ensure that such tanks are cleaned and disinfected at least once every 12 months, in accordance with the Code of Practice on Environmental Health. After cleaning, the tank should be disinfected with a chlorine solution and flushed thoroughly before the supply is restored. Premises owners are also encouraged to keep records of tank cleaning dates for inspection by relevant authorities.

**1. WATER QUALITY ADVISORY – SCHEDULED MAINS FLUSHING IN THE BEDOK AND KEMBANGAN AREAS**

The Board wishes to inform residents and business operators in the Bedok and Kembangan areas that scheduled flushing of water mains will be carried out from **17 May 2021 to 28 May 2021**, between the hours of **10.00 p.m. and 5.00 a.m.** The flushing is part of PUB's routine maintenance programme to ensure the continued quality of water supplied through the distribution network.

(b) A slight drop in water pressure. This is temporary and will be resolved upon completion of the flushing works in the respective zones.

(c) Intermittent water supply interruptions of up to **30 minutes** in some zones. PUB and its contractors will make every effort to minimise the duration of any interruption.

Residents with medical conditions that require a continuous supply of water (e.g., dialysis patients) are advised to make the necessary arrangements, such as storing water in advance. PUB apologises for any inconvenience caused.

For enquiries or feedback, residents may contact the PUB Water Quality Feedback Line at **1800-225-5782** or submit a request via the PUB mobile application. Alternatively, they may approach the PUB officers present at the worksites during the flushing hours.

Following the completion of the flushing works, PUB will conduct post-flushing water quality verification in the affected areas. The verification will involve sampling and testing at selected consumer taps, as well as at fire hydrants and other points in the distribution network within the flushing zones.

The parameters to be tested include, but are not limited to, turbidity, pH, residual chlorine, and the presence of total coliforms and *E. coli*. The results of these tests will be published in the next quarterly water quality report on the PUB website.

PUB reminds residents that the water supplied by PUB complies with the Environmental Public Health (Water Quality) Regulations and the WHO Guidelines for Drinking-water Quality. PUB will arrange for a site visit and sampling at the tap upon request.

Such items do not break down in water and can cause blockages in the sewerage system, leading to sewage backflow and flooding in homes and public areas.

**4. NOTICE OF ACCREDITATION OF WATER QUALITY LABORATORY**

The Public Utilities Board (PUB) wishes to inform the public that the PUB Water Quality Laboratory has been granted accreditation by the Singapore Accreditation Council (SAC) under the Singapore Laboratory Accreditation Scheme (SAC-SINGLAS) for its testing capabilities. The accreditation certificate, number LA-2023-0841, was issued on 15 September 2023 and is valid for a period of four years, subject to annual surveillance audits conducted by SAC.

The scope of accreditation covers the following test methods, which are used in the routine monitoring of drinking water quality:

The accreditation affirms PUB's commitment to maintaining rigorous quality standards in its testing procedures. The laboratory has undergone a comprehensive assessment of its quality management system, technical competence, and testing procedures. The assessment included on-site observations of sample handling, instrument calibration, and data management practices.

Copies of the accreditation certificate and the detailed scope of accreditation are available for inspection at the PUB Water Quality Laboratory, 40 Scotts Road, #20-01, Singapore 228231, during office hours (9:00 am to 5:00 pm, Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays). **5. IMPLEMENTATION OF ENHANCED TESTING PROCEDURES FOR MICROPLASTIC ANALYSIS**

PUB will be implementing enhanced testing procedures for the analysis of microplastics in raw and treated water samples. These procedures will be effective from 1 October 2023 and will be applied to samples collected from all water treatment plants and selected points in the distribution network.

The new procedures involve the use of Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) for the identification and quantification of microplastic particles. The method allows for the detection of particles in the size range of 20 micrometres to 5 millimetres. The procedures have been developed in consultation with international partners and are aligned with the methodologies recommended by the World Health Organization in its 2019 report on microplastics in drinking-water.

Sampling frequency will be increased from quarterly to monthly at the water treatment plants, while sampling at distribution network points will remain on a quarterly basis. The results of the microplastic analysis will be included in the annual water quality report, with the first set of results expected to be published in the second quarter of 2024.

The Board emphasises that the presence of microplastics in drinking water is not currently known to pose a health risk at the levels detected. The implementation of these enhanced procedures is part of PUB's ongoing efforts to stay abreast of emerging contaminants and to provide assurance to the public regarding the safety of Singapore's water supply.

**6. WATER QUALITY REPORTING AND DATA MANAGEMENT FRAMEWORK**

PUB wishes to inform all stakeholders that the revised Water Quality Reporting and Data Management Framework will take effect from 1 January 2024. The framework consolidates the existing reporting obligations under the Public Utilities (Water Supply) Regulations and introduces a unified template for the submission of water quality data by licensed water service providers.

Key revisions include the standardisation of reporting intervals for microbiological and physicochemical parameters, the introduction of a digital submission portal, and the alignment of data fields with the national water quality database. Licensed water service providers are required to submit their data on a monthly basis, with the first submission under the new framework due by 15 February 2024.

The Board notes that the framework does not introduce new water quality standards but rather harmonises the manner in which existing standards are monitored and reported. Providers who require clarification on the submission requirements may contact the Water Quality Department at [wqd_regulatory@pub.gov.sg](mailto:wqd_regulatory@pub.gov.sg) or 1800-284-6600.

The report will include the results of routine water quality monitoring, a summary of compliance with the Environmental Public Health (Water Quality) Regulations, and a section on emerging contaminants, including the first set of microplastic analysis results under the enhanced testing procedures implemented in October 2023.

Members of the public who wish to provide feedback on the report may do so through the online feedback form on the PUB website. Feedback received by 31 May 2024 will be considered for the next annual report.

The Water Safety Plan (WSP) for the public water supply system was first adopted in 2016 and has been reviewed on a three-year cycle. 5. Notice of Public Consultation – Water Tariff Review
The Board invites members of the public and interested stakeholders to submit feedback on the proposed water tariff adjustments for the 2020-2022 period. The consultation period will run from 25 July 2019 to 25 August 2019. Written submissions may be sent to the Board via email at tariff_review@pub.gov.sg, or by post to the address above, marked "Attention: Tariff Review Committee." All feedback received will be considered prior to the finalisation of the tariff proposal, which will be submitted to the Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment for approval.

6. Operational Update – Choa Chu Kang Waterworks
The Board wishes to provide an update on the operational status of the Choa Chu Kang Waterworks. The plant continues to operate in accordance with its approved design parameters, and routine inspections have confirmed that all treatment processes are functioning within normal ranges. Choa Chu Kang Waterworks treatment_capacity 160000 m3/day. Record status: current. This capacity figure reflects the current approved maximum daily throughput of the plant, as recorded in the Board's engineering records, and will remain in effect until further notice. No changes to the plant's operational capacity are anticipated in the upcoming financial year.

7. Advisory – Water Tank Cleaning in Private Premises
The Board reminds owners of residential and commercial premises with water storage tanks to ensure that such tanks are cleaned and disinfected at least once every 12 months, in accordance with the Code of Practice on Environmental Health. Cleaning should be carried out by licensed plumbers or certified tank-cleaning contractors. After cleaning, the tank should be disinfected with a chlorine solution and flushed thoroughly before the supply is restored. Premises owners are also encouraged to keep records of tank cleaning dates for inspection by relevant authorities.

8. Correction Notice – Publication of Maintenance Schedule
The Board wishes to correct an error in the maintenance schedule published on 15 July 2019, which incorrectly listed the dates for the routine maintenance of the Kranji Waterworks. The correct dates are 19 August 2019 to 23 August 2019, not 12 August 2019 to 16 August 2019 as previously stated. The Board apologises for any inconvenience caused by this error. The maintenance works at Kranji Waterworks will proceed as corrected, and affected customers will be notified individually if any supply interruption is required.

9. Invitation for Tender – Supply of Water Quality Testing Reagents
The Board invites tenders from qualified suppliers for the supply and delivery of water quality testing reagents, including but not limited to chemical reagents for pH, chlorine, and turbidity analysis. Tenders shall be submitted in sealed envelopes marked "Tender No. PUB/2019/T-045" and deposited in the tender box at the PUB headquarters by 12:00 p.m. on 30 August 2019. Tender documents may be obtained from the Procurement Department upon payment of a non-refundable fee of S$50.00. The Board is pleased to announce the launch of the Shower Head Replacement Programme, a new initiative under the larger Water Efficiency Drive. Under this programme, households that have not replaced their shower heads in the last five years may apply for a one-time replacement with a water-efficient model. The new shower heads are expected to reduce water consumption by up to 15% per shower.

Applications will open on 1 April 2022 and close on 30 September 2022, or until the allocated stock is exhausted. Interested households may apply via the PUB website or through the mobile application. Each household is limited to two replacement units. Installation is to be carried out by the applicant, and replacement units will be delivered to the registered address within four to six weeks of successful application.

3. PUBLIC CONSULTATION ON WATER PRICING REVIEW

The Board has commenced a public consultation on the proposed review of water pricing structures. The consultation is part of the Board's ongoing effort to ensure that water tariffs remain sustainable and reflective of the full cost of water production, treatment, and distribution. Members of the public are invited to share their views on the proposed pricing framework, which includes considerations for tiered tariffs for domestic users and a revised approach to non-domestic water charges.

The consultation documents are available on the PUB website and at all public libraries. Written feedback may be submitted via the online portal, by post, or by email to consultation@pub.gov.sg. The consultation period will run from 1 April 2022 to 31 May 2022. The Board will review all feedback received and publish a summary of the findings by August 2022.

4. ANNOUNCEMENT – JURONG ISLAND WATER RECLAMATION PLANT

The Board wishes to provide an update on the operations of the Jurong Island Water Reclamation Plant. The plant continues to operate as a key facility for the treatment of industrial water on Jurong Island, supporting the water needs of the petrochemical and refining industries located there. As part of the Board's regular review of its water infrastructure, the following information is recorded in the current controlled registry of plant capabilities:

Jurong Island Water Reclamation Plant treatment_capacity 250000 m3/day. Record status: current.

This figure reflects the plant's current design capacity and remains unchanged since the last review. No changes to the plant's operational capacity are anticipated in the upcoming financial year. The Board will continue to monitor the plant's performance and will provide further updates should there be any changes to its operational parameters.

5. CORRECTION NOTICE – WATER REBATE SCHEDULE FOR FY2021

The Board wishes to correct an error in the water rebate schedule published on 15 January 2021, which incorrectly listed the rebate amount for 4-room HDB flats. The correct amount is S$25 per quarter, not S$20 per quarter as previously stated. Households that were under-rebated as a result of this error will have the difference credited to their accounts automatically. The Board apologises for any inconvenience caused by this error.

6. ADVISORY – WATER CONSERVATION DURING DRY WEATHER

The Board advises all water users to exercise water conservation measures in light of the current dry weather conditions. Members of the public are encouraged to:

(a) take shorter showers;
   (b) use a basin when washing dishes or vegetables;

**1. WATER QUALITY ADVISORY – SCHEDULED MAINS FLUSHING IN THE BEDOK AND KEMBANGAN AREAS**

The Board wishes to inform residents and business operators in the Bedok and Kembangan areas that scheduled flushing of water mains will be carried out from **17 May 2021 to 28 May 2021**, between the hours of **10.00 p.m. and 5.00 a.m.** The flushing is part of PUB's routine maintenance programme to ensure the continued quality of water supplied through the distribution network.

During the flushing period, residents in the affected areas may experience the following:

(a) Temporary discolouration of water due to the disturbance of sediments in the pipes. This is not a health concern. Should discolouration occur, residents are advised to run the tap for a few minutes until the water runs clear before use.

(b) A slight drop in water pressure. This is temporary and will be resolved upon completion of the flushing works in the respective zones.

(c) Intermittent water supply interruptions of up to **30 minutes** in some zones. PUB and its contractors will make every effort to minimise the duration of any interruption.

The affected areas are bounded by Bedok North Avenue 3, Upper Changi Road East, Bedok South Avenue 1, and the Pan Island Expressway (PIE). A detailed list of the specific blocks and streets within the flushing zones is annexed to this notice and is also available on the PUB website.

Residents with medical conditions that require a continuous supply of water (e.g., dialysis patients) are advised to make the necessary arrangements, such as storing water in advance. PUB apologises for any inconvenience caused.

For enquiries or feedback, residents may contact the PUB Water Quality Feedback Line at **1800-225-5782** or submit a request via the PUB mobile application. Alternatively, they may approach the PUB officers present at the worksites during the flushing hours.

**2. NOTICE OF WATER QUALITY TESTING AT TAP – POST-FLUSHING VERIFICATION**

Following the completion of the flushing works, PUB will conduct post-flushing water quality verification in the affected areas. The verification will involve sampling and testing at selected consumer taps, as well as at fire hydrants and other points in the distribution network within the flushing zones.

The parameters to be tested include, but are not limited to, turbidity, pH, residual chlorine, and the presence of total coliforms and *E. coli*. The results of these tests will be published in the next quarterly water quality report on the PUB website.

PUB reminds residents that the water supplied by PUB complies with the Environmental Public Health (Water Quality) Regulations and the WHO Guidelines for Drinking-water Quality. Should residents have any concerns about the water quality in their premises after the flushing period, they may contact PUB at the number above. PUB will arrange for a site visit and sampling at the tap upon request.

**3. REMINDER – PROPER DISPOSAL OF WIPES AND SANITARY PRODUCTS**

The Board takes this opportunity to remind all members of the public that wet wipes, sanitary pads, and other non-flushable items must not be flushed down the toilet or disposed of in the sink. Such items do not break down in water and can cause blockages in the sewerage system, leading to sewage backflow and flooding in homes and public areas.

**4. NOTICE OF ACCREDITATION OF WATER QUALITY LABORATORY**

The Public Utilities Board (PUB) wishes to inform the public that the PUB Water Quality Laboratory has been granted accreditation by the Singapore Accreditation Council (SAC) under the Singapore Laboratory Accreditation Scheme (SAC-SINGLAS) for its testing capabilities. The accreditation certificate, number LA-2023-0841, was issued on 15 September 2023 and is valid for a period of four years, subject to annual surveillance audits conducted by SAC.

The scope of accreditation covers the following test methods, which are used in the routine monitoring of drinking water quality:

| **Test Parameter** | **Test Method Reference** | **Accredited Range** |
|---------------------|---------------------------|----------------------|
| pH | APHA 4500-H+ B | 4.0 – 10.0 |
| Turbidity | APHA 2130 B | 0.05 – 100 NTU |
| Residual Chlorine (Free) | APHA 4500-Cl G | 0.02 – 5.0 mg/L |
| Total Coliforms | APHA 9222 B | Presence/Absence |
| *E. coli* | APHA 9222 D | Presence/Absence |
| Conductivity | APHA 2510 B | 10 – 2000 µS/cm |
| Total Dissolved Solids | APHA 2540 C | 10 – 1000 mg/L |

The accreditation affirms PUB's commitment to maintaining rigorous quality standards in its testing procedures. The laboratory has undergone a comprehensive assessment of its quality management system, technical competence, and testing procedures. The assessment included on-site observations of sample handling, instrument calibration, and data management practices.

Copies of the accreditation certificate and the detailed scope of accreditation are available for inspection at the PUB Water Quality Laboratory, 40 Scotts Road, #20-01, Singapore 228231, during office hours (9:00 am to 5:00 pm, Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays). Members of the public may also request copies via email at [pub_wqlab@pub.gov.sg](mailto:pub_wqlab@pub.gov.sg).

**5. IMPLEMENTATION OF ENHANCED TESTING PROCEDURES FOR MICROPLASTIC ANALYSIS**

PUB will be implementing enhanced testing procedures for the analysis of microplastics in raw and treated water samples. These procedures will be effective from 1 October 2023 and will be applied to samples collected from all water treatment plants and selected points in the distribution network.

The new procedures involve the use of Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) for the identification and quantification of microplastic particles. The method allows for the detection of particles in the size range of 20 micrometres to 5 millimetres. The procedures have been developed in consultation with international partners and are aligned with the methodologies recommended by the World Health Organization in its 2019 report on microplastics in drinking-water.

Sampling frequency will be increased from quarterly to monthly at the water treatment plants, while sampling at distribution network points will remain on a quarterly basis. The results of the microplastic analysis will be included in the annual water quality report, with the first set of results expected to be published in the second quarter of 2024.

The Board emphasises that the presence of microplastics in drinking water is not currently known to pose a health risk at the levels detected. The implementation of these enhanced procedures is part of PUB's ongoing efforts to stay abreast of emerging contaminants and to provide assurance to the public regarding the safety of Singapore's water supply.

**6. WATER QUALITY REPORTING AND DATA MANAGEMENT FRAMEWORK**

PUB wishes to inform all stakeholders that the revised Water Quality Reporting and Data Management Framework will take effect from 1 January 2024. The framework consolidates the existing reporting obligations under the Public Utilities (Water Supply) Regulations and introduces a unified template for the submission of water quality data by licensed water service providers.

The WSP is a risk-based management tool that identifies potential hazards in the water supply system, from catchment to tap, and establishes control measures to mitigate those hazards. The revised plan incorporates lessons learned from the 2023 dry season, operational feedback from the treatment plants, and the findings of the internal audit conducted in November 2023.

PUB invites members of the public to provide feedback on the draft Water Safety Plan. The draft plan is available for inspection at the following locations from 18 March 2024 to 15 April 2024:
